feat(ui): import, place and pick a tool body in the tool editor; draw it in the simulation

The tool editor gains a Body column: Import body… (STEP/STL/OBJ) and
Clear body, the axis (six presets or a picked face normal), the tip
offset, Pick tip / Pick axis on an egui-painted orbitable 3D preview,
a live placement note, and Apply body, which queues one SetToolBody
(undoable; refusals land on the Tool pane by name). Picks and orbit are
ephemeral. The profile preview overlays the placed body's envelope.

While the simulation runs, the running tool's body is posed at the
playhead and drawn as a model part; tools without a body add nothing.

App helpers live in app::tool_body_view (load, presets, preview, pick,
tip offset, posing, body of an operation's tool).

Fixes #371

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(ui): draw the whole tool in the simulation when it has a body, and frame it

On a real document the body was posed a shank length above the tip
with nothing below it, off the top of a part-framed view, so the
simulation looked the same with and without it. A tool with a body now
draws whole while simulating - cutter and shank revolved from its
numbers up into the body (app::tool_body_view::assembly) - at every
playhead, paused or playing, stale or fresh; Frame takes the posed
assembly in. Tools without a body draw exactly as before.

Pinned on the user's own document (step_block_371.camproj fixture).

Refs #371

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(ui): leave Frame's extent to the document while simulating

The previous commit also folded the posed tool assembly into Frame
while the transport was up. On the user's word the view behaviour stays
as it was (zoom out to see a tall holder); the whole-tool drawing of a
tool with a body stays. The regression test keeps its whole-tool,
every-playhead, stale-and-fresh checks.

Refs #371

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(ui): zoom and fit the tool editor's 3D body preview

Wheel or pinch (Ctrl+wheel) over the preview zooms about the cursor,
clamped to 1/4x..32x of the fit view; double-click or the new Fit
button resets orbit, zoom and pan. Drag still orbits. View state only.
The decision file records the zoom and the whole-tool simulation
drawing.

Refs #371

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(ui): the simulation draws the tool and its holder cylinder when it has no body

The running tool is now always drawn at the playhead: cutter and shank
revolved from Tool::profile, then the modelled body when it has one,
else the holder cylinder from its own numbers (holder_d x holder_len on
the shank top - the HolderStack::cylinder reading the collision laws
judge). The lathe insert kinds keep the axis marker only: their profile
is a stand-in envelope. Tests and the decision file follow.

Refs #371

feat(tools): spun holder-profile editor for milling tools

A milling tool's holder can now be drawn as a revolved half-outline
(points tip-up, straight or arc segments) in the tool editor's new
Profile tab: Parametric (the holder cylinder of the numbers) or Custom
(hand edits), a flat to-scale side view with flute/stickout/gauge
dimensions, live refusals by name, and Apply profile - one undoable
SetToolBody::spun. The drawn holder lands as a ToolBody whose envelope
is the outline's exact bands (arcs flattened conservatively), so every
#368 law, the stamp and the sim assembly read it. Saved as an optional
`spun` key beside the facets (no project rung: a reader without it
judges the facets, which can only over-report). Turning tools keep the
Body section alone. Custom cutter/shank profiles are a follow-up.

Refs #93

Merge remote-tracking branch 'upstream/main' (#381, #395, #431, #422, #407, #420, #461) into issue/371-tool-body-ui

Conflicts:
- crates/app/src/commands/mod.rs: kept both re-exports - main's
  `LatheBodySpec` joins `SetToolBody, ToolBodySpec`, and this branch's
  `ImportReport, ImportTools` stays.
- crates/app/src/lib.rs: kept both modules - this branch's
  `tool_body_view` (#371) and main's `tool_body_lathe` (#369).

Semantic fix-ups for #395's `ToolBody::frame` (the `profile` field is now
the `ToolBody::profile()` read, `None` for a lathe-frame body):
- tool_body_view::assembly carries the shank to the body's foot only for
  a spindle body; assembly_for_operation draws the bare tool for a
  lathe-frame body (its facets sit in the turning frame, not the
  spindle frame the assembly draws in).
- ui tool_body_page reads the envelope/foot-top note through profile().
- tests/tool_body_view reads profile() on the spindle bodies it builds.

Merge branch 'issue/371-tool-body-ui' (main at 5fd2b93a: #381, #395, #431, #422, #407, #420, #461) into issue/93-spun-tool-editor

Conflicts:
- crates/tools/src/lib.rs: kept all modules - `spun` (#93) beside main's
  `lathe_holder` (#369) and `lathe_insert_zone` (#396).
- crates/app/src/schema.rs: ToolBody carries both main's `frame:
  BodyFrame` (Spindle / Lathe, replacing axis/offset/profile) and this
  branch's `spun: Option<SpunProfile>`; `ToolBody::profile()` stays the
  spindle-envelope read.
- crates/app/src/tool_body.rs: both imports; `build` lands
  `BodyFrame::Spindle { .. }` with `spun: None`; `build_spun` now builds
  a spindle-frame body (axis +Z, offset 0, the profile's exact bands).
- crates/app/src/project/tool_body_wire.rs: ToolBodyDto keeps main's
  optional `axis`/`offset`, `lathe` and `insert_zone` keys AND the
  additive `spun` key. from_body writes `spun` on a spindle body and
  never on a lathe one; to_body re-draws a `spun` body first and
  refuses `spun` beside `lathe`/`insert_zone` by name, else main's
  spindle/lathe dispatch. Module doc keeps all three notes.

Semantic fix-ups: tool_body_lathe::build sets `spun: None`;
tool_body_view::spun_preview's probe body takes a spindle frame;
tests/tool_spun_profile reads `profile()` instead of the old field.
